correctness.rationale: The recent source defines \(\Gamma(K)\) as minimum first Betti number over all spanning surfaces and states that an orientable spanning surface of a knot has first Betti number \(2g\). Its Theorem 1.4 gives \(\overline\Gamma(c)=c/3+1/9+o(1)\) on the mirror-distinguishing ensemble. Suzuki--Tran give \(\overline g(c)=c/4+1/12+o(1)\) on the same convention. Hence linearity of averaging gives \(\overline D(c)=c/6+1/18+o(1)\). Since \(0\le D(K)/c<1\), the threshold inequality \(E[X]\le\delta+(1-\delta)P(X\ge\delta)\) gives the stated liminf bound. No finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The quantity \(D(K)=2g(K)-\Gamma(K)\) is not an arbitrary combination: both terms are minimum first Betti numbers for the same spanning-surface problem, with and without the orientability constraint. The result shows that this topological constraint costs \(c/6+o(c)\) on average and, unlike a mere ratio of averages, forces a positive asymptotic fraction of individual 2-bridge knots to pay a linear cost. This gives a structural prevalence statement about spanning surfaces that neither marginal-average theorem supplies.
